conceptZh: 螃蟹有兩隻大鉗子，橫著走
object: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet and a little red crab
morph: the astronaut builds a wrong space-rocket shape first, then rebuilds it into 蟹
creativeAngle: 太空人玩偶先拼出火箭、再發現不對，改成螃蟹拼出字。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蟹 (crab). Lead: a bouncy white astronaut toy with a round fishbowl helmet who floats up off the ground whenever he jumps. Moment 1 (0-1.6s): he proudly stacks red stroke parts into a pointed rocket and zooms upward, helmet bumping a ceiling-high cloud as the voice says 蟹. Moment 2 (1.6-3.3s): he notices the rocket is wrong, shrugs, floats down and swaps the pieces with a fast shuffle; at the second 蟹 the parts click into 蟹. Moment 3 (3.3-5s): a small round red crab scuttles sideways across the sand floor to the glyph, claws raised; the voice says 螃蟹 as the astronaut floats up and nose-to-claw with it, the crab pinches his antenna with a harmless boing. Moment 4 (5-8s): glyph still; the astronaut bobs gently while the crab dances sideways. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蟹、蟹、螃蟹" (ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄆㄤˊ ㄒㄧㄝˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蟹, drawn as saturated solid coral red strokes on a pale sky blue background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.
